handoff: Review #1: approve. Backlog issue rows (CP2), story take (GR1), RemotePort listLabelledIssues/assignIssue with contract tests, TUI refresh cadence and docs all match the spec. Unit tier, typecheck, story-take and status-watch integration green. Minor only: --json drops a failed backlog read silently; glab backlog capped at 100; backlog re-read after a story-row take.

findings.title: `status --watch --json` drops a failed backlog read silently
findings.detail:
`readBacklog(ctx).catch(() => null)` turns a remote failure into a model with no issue rows and no sign that the read failed, so a front end reading CP5 JSON cannot tell 'no backlog' from 'remote down'. The TUI path says so in the footer (CP6); the JSON path has no equivalent.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Carry a flag or error string in the model (e.g. header.backlog_error) or document in CP5 that the issues are best effort.

findings.title: glab backlog is capped at 100 issues (gh at 500)
findings.detail:
listLabelledIssues uses `--per-page 100` with no pagination, mirroring listAssignedIssues; a GitLab project with more than 100 open norn issues shows a truncated backlog. Unassigned issues are the larger set, so the cap bites earlier here than for intake.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Raise the per-page or page through; fine to leave as a follow-up.

findings.title: Backlog re-read after any take, including a story checkout
findings.detail:
`if (action.id === "take") backlogAt = null` also fires for the story-row take (`story checkout`), costing one extra remote read; harmless.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Check `row.kind === "issue"` if the extra read matters.
